articles.title: The Defense Contract Management Agency's Resource Workload Model Ecosystem: A Basis for Enhanced Warfighter Support
articles.summary: This RAND report evaluates the Defense Contract Management Agency’s (DCMA) Integrated Resource Workload Model (IRWM), concluding that while it is a robust tool for aggregate manpower planning, it requires significant refinements to better reflect operational realities. Based on over 225 interviews and an in-depth review of the model's structure, researchers identified discrepancies between modeled estimates and actual field activities, often stemming from insufficient documentation, unmodeled supervisory tasks, and user-unfriendly data entry systems. To maximize the model's utility, the report recommends formalizing standard operating procedures, improving internal communication to build trust, and leveraging the modeling ecosystem for strategic scenario planning regarding budget and mission shifts.

articles.title: A Typology of Economic Shocks and Applications for Macroeconomic Analysis
articles.summary: The report introduces a unified typology of 20 economic shocks across five domains to help analysts understand and anticipate macroeconomic recessions as complex, compound events. By examining the Great Recession and the COVID-19 pandemic, the authors demonstrate how the interaction of exogenous disturbances and endogenous policy responses determines the recovery's trajectory. This analytical framework moves beyond traditional siloed approaches, providing a structured method for modeling the cascading effects of financial, environmental, and demand-side disruptions. Consequently, it serves as a critical resource for policymakers to improve real-time situational awareness and calibrate stabilization efforts more effectively during multi-faceted crises.

articles.title: Improving Diffusion of Clinical Care Innovations in Public Health Emergencies: 5 Things Influential Emergency Department Clinicians on Digital Media Can Do
articles.summary: This RAND report outlines five strategic actions for influential emergency department clinicians on digital media to enhance the rapid and effective diffusion of clinical care innovations during public health emergencies. Drawing on a four-year study of the COVID-19 pandemic—including focus groups, interviews, and surveys of over 1,600 healthcare professionals—the researchers emphasize the necessity of transparency, collaborative partnerships with medical societies, and multimedia "how-to" content. Implementing these strategies aims to mitigate the uneven adoption of medical advancements and ensure a more synchronized, evidence-based healthcare response to future crises.

zh.summary: 這份蘭德公司（RAND）報告針對在數位媒體上具影響力的急診科臨床醫師，提出五項策略行動，旨在強化公共衛生緊急狀態期間臨床照護創新的快速且有效傳播。研究人員針對 COVID-19 疫情進行為期四年的研究，包含焦點小組、訪談以及對 1,600 多名醫療專業人員的問卷調查；基於此研究，報告強調了透明度、與醫學學會建立合作夥伴關係，以及提供多媒體「實務操作」內容的必要性。實施這些策略旨在改善醫療進展採用不均的問題，並確保未來面對危機時，能做出更同步且實證導向的醫療照護反應。

articles.title: Improving Diffusion of Clinical Care Innovations in Public Health Emergencies: 6 Things Frontline Emergency Department Clinicians Can Do
articles.summary: Frontline emergency department (ED) clinicians can play a pivotal role in accelerating the adoption of clinical innovations and retiring ineffective practices during public health emergencies by engaging in proactive networking and evidence-sharing. This RAND study, based on a four-year analysis of COVID-19 responses including surveys of over 1,600 healthcare professionals, identifies six specific strategies across pre-emergency and active-emergency phases. To bolster future pandemic resilience, health systems and policymakers must support clinician-led initiatives such as interprofessional information networks and bedside evidence-informed decision-making tools to ensure more agile and equitable care delivery.

articles.title: Improving Diffusion of Clinical Care Innovations in Public Health Emergencies: 5 Things Emergency Department and Health System Leaders Can Do
articles.summary: This RAND report identifies five key strategies for health system and emergency department leaders to accelerate the adoption of clinical care innovations during public health emergencies. Drawing on focus groups and a nationwide survey of over 1,600 clinicians, the study found that innovation diffusion was often uneven and outpaced by the COVID-19 pandemic’s spread. Strategic recommendations include establishing pre-emergency communication networks, creating dedicated teams for 'living' evidence-based guidance, and utilizing real-time dashboards to monitor operating conditions. These actions aim to bridge the gap between emerging evidence and frontline practice, ensuring that health systems can rapidly implement effective treatments while discontinuing harmful ones during future crises.

articles.title: State-Level Impacts of Key Medicaid Provisions in the One Big Beautiful Bill Act
articles.summary: This RAND report analyzes the state-level effects of the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBBA), estimating a $664 billion reduction in state Medicaid budgets and a loss of 7.6 million enrollees by 2034. The analysis shows that expansion states with high reliance on provider taxes and state-directed payments, such as California and Arizona, will face the most significant financial disruptions. While the Rural Health Transformation Program provides some relief for smaller states, most will struggle with federal funding gaps, likely forcing cuts to services or eligibility. These findings suggest that the act shifts substantial fiscal and administrative burdens to states, potentially increasing uncompensated care and limiting access to health services.

articles.title: Improving Diffusion of Clinical Care Innovations in Public Health Emergencies: 6 Things Journal and Preprint Editors Can Do
articles.summary: This RAND report outlines six practical strategies for journal and preprint editors to accelerate the diffusion of clinical care innovations during public health emergencies. Based on a four-year study of COVID-19 pandemic responses, the findings emphasize the need to prioritize implementation materials, leverage microcontent for wider reach, and establish accelerated yet high-quality peer-review pathways. Implementing these measures would bridge the gap between emerging evidence and clinical practice, ensuring front-line clinicians can safely and rapidly adopt life-saving innovations while minimizing the spread of misinformation.

articles.title: Improving Diffusion of Clinical Care Innovations in Public Health Emergencies: 7 Things Leaders of Professional Societies Can Do
articles.summary: Professional societies must take a proactive role in coordinating and disseminating clinical innovations to improve emergency department responses during public health emergencies. Based on a four-year study of the COVID-19 pandemic, RAND identifies seven key strategies, including the creation of living guidance documents and clinician-only virtual spaces for information sharing. These actions are designed to reduce conflicting messaging and bridge the gap between emerging evidence and frontline practice, ensuring faster adoption of effective care strategies.

articles.title: Improving Diffusion of Clinical Care Innovations in Public Health Emergencies: 4 Things State and Local Public Health Officials Can Do
articles.summary: This RAND report identifies critical strategies for state and local public health officials to accelerate the diffusion of clinical care innovations in emergency departments during future public health emergencies. Drawing on a four-year study of COVID-19 responses, the research highlights that established communication infrastructure and trust between public health agencies and frontline clinicians are essential for overcoming fragmented data sharing and uneven adoption of new treatments. To improve preparedness, officials are encouraged to establish regular touchpoints with regional health systems during non-emergency periods and develop standardized data-sharing platforms to facilitate real-time learning across diverse practice settings. Providing locally tailored guidance further empowers clinicians to engage in evidence-informed decision-making at the bedside, ensuring that effective innovations reach patients more consistently.

articles.title: After the strike: The danger of war in Iran
articles.summary: Brookings experts argue that the U.S.-Israeli decapitation strike against Iran’s leadership is unlikely to trigger an immediate regime collapse, risking instead a protracted conflict and regional instability. The analysis highlights the resilience of the Islamic Republic's institutional networks and its escalatory survival strategy, which targets neighboring energy infrastructure to force diplomatic concessions. Policymakers are warned that without a coherent 'day after' plan or the integration of civilian statecraft, the intervention could lead to a 'lose-lose' scenario of state fragmentation and emboldened global adversaries.

articles.title: What to look out for at this year’s meeting of China’s legislature
articles.summary: The upcoming National People’s Congress (NPC) will formally launch China’s 15th Five-Year Plan, prioritizing technological self-sufficiency and 'high-quality' manufacturing to mitigate U.S.-led export controls. Key initiatives include strategic investments in AI, quantum computing, and the 'low-altitude economy,' alongside new legislation codifying the Communist Party’s direct oversight of national development planning. These efforts aim to project a narrative of domestic stability and 'orderly' governance as Beijing prepares for a high-stakes summit with U.S. President Donald Trump. Consequently, the international community should anticipate a China increasingly focused on reducing foreign dependencies while consolidating centralized political control over its economic future.

articles.title: Now what? The limits of tariff-driven economic statecraft after IEEPA
articles.summary: Following a Supreme Court ruling invalidating the use of the International Emergency Economic Powers Act (IEEPA) for broad tariffs, the U.S. administration has pivoted to alternative statutory authorities, signaling that high tariffs remain a permanent policy fixture rather than a temporary emergency measure. This shift highlights a growing tension where tariffs are increasingly used as a primary tool for both fiscal revenue and industrial policy, despite inherent contradictions between maximizing tax collection and incentivizing domestic reshoring. Experts warn that broad tariffs function as blunt instruments that can erode the competitiveness of domestic manufacturers embedded in global value chains while inducing allies to diversify away from U.S. economic volatility. To achieve lasting resilience, the analysis suggests transitioning from unilateral trade measures toward targeted industrial subsidies and coordinated supply chain initiatives with trusted international partners.

articles.title: Why Texas could determine which party controls the Senate in 2027
articles.summary: The outcome of the Texas Republican Senate runoff between incumbent John Cornyn and Attorney General Ken Paxton may determine party control of the U.S. Senate in 2027. Democratic nominee James Talarico has emerged as a formidable challenger, demonstrating high voter mobilization and significant appeal among the state's crucial Hispanic swing vote. While a Cornyn victory in May likely secures the seat for Republicans, a Paxton win would create a highly competitive general election that could end a three-decade Democratic drought in statewide Texas races.

Democratic nominee James Talarico has emerged as a formidable challenger, demonstrating high voter mobilization and significant appeal among the state's crucial Hispanic swing vote. While a Cornyn victory in May likely secures the seat for Republicans, a Paxton win would create a highly competitive general election that could end a three-decade Democratic drought in statewide Texas races.

articles.title: After the ‘fork’: Greater Washington leads the nation in regional job loss
articles.summary: The Greater Washington (DMV) region recorded the highest employment decline among major U.S. metro areas in 2025, primarily driven by massive federal workforce reductions that eliminated approximately 54,000 positions. This 1.7% total job loss was exacerbated by a contracting private sector that failed to absorb displaced workers, leading to unemployment spikes that disproportionately impacted Black workers and women. The findings highlight the federal government's role as an indispensable regional economic anchor and suggest that mitigating this 'industry shock' will require intensive cross-sector collaboration and targeted investment.

articles.title: What’s next for the Iran war? Experts discuss.
articles.summary: Brookings experts argue that the Trump administration’s military campaign against Iran lacks a coherent long-term strategy and clear objectives, shifting from nuclear containment to regime change without adequate planning for the resulting power vacuum. While conventional strikes were initially successful, the U.S. remains vulnerable to asymmetric threats like drones and faces massive logistical challenges in evacuating hundreds of thousands of citizens from the region. Analysts emphasize the need for an immediate diplomatic 'off-ramp' and a realistic plan for dealing with a weakened but still-entrenched Iranian regime to avoid prolonged regional instability.

articles.title: The surreal experience of meeting Khamenei
articles.summary: Ambassador Jeffrey Feltman reflects on his 2012 meeting with Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, highlighting the Supreme Leader's paranoid obsession with United States 'enmity' and his conviction that America was a declining, malicious power. During the encounter, Khamenei ignored standard diplomatic topics to deliver a lengthy monologue indicting U.S. foreign policy and predicting its internal collapse, dismissing diplomatic overtures as deceptive ruses. This rigid ideological hostility drove Iran’s regional proxy warfare and nuclear ambitions, indicating that Khamenei viewed negotiations primarily as a tactical means to buy time. The reflection underscores how the Supreme Leader's unshakeable distrust shaped decades of Iranian policy, persisting through major escalations until his death in early 2026.

articles.title: Iraq must not be a staging ground for war with Iran
articles.summary: Iraq faces a critical threat of internal collapse as it becomes an involuntary staging ground for escalating hostilities between Iran, Israel, and the United States following the assassination of Ali Khamenei. Despite a weakened interim government, Iraqi political and religious leaders like Grand Ayatollah Sistani are striving to maintain neutrality to prevent a descent into multi-front civil conflict involving various paramilitary and ethnic groups. The country's stability is currently jeopardized by retaliatory strikes on its soil and disruptions to vital oil and electricity infrastructure. Consequently, the United States should avoid escalatory military actions within Iraq and prioritize diplomatic partnerships to preserve the country's role as a regional stabilizer.

articles.title: How is China positioning itself as Iran’s regime teeters?
articles.summary: Brookings argues that China’s relationship with Iran is characterized by "strategic opportunism," prioritizing Chinese domestic stability and energy security over the survival of the current Iranian regime. While Beijing benefits from discounted oil and Iran’s role in diverting U.S. resources, it remains pragmatic and notably failed to provide tangible security support during recent U.S. strikes on Iranian nuclear sites. Consequently, China is prepared to adapt to a potential regime collapse by engaging any successor to prevent a pro-American pivot, while simultaneously intensifying domestic surveillance to suppress any "color revolution" sentiments inspired by Iranian protests.

articles.title: USMCA Forward 2026
articles.summary: The Brookings 2026 USMCA Forward report argues that the upcoming joint review of the trade agreement is a critical juncture for North American partners to address structural strains and enhance regional competitiveness. Through analyses of key sectors like automotive, steel, and pharmaceuticals, the report highlights how increased economic integration persists despite political friction and supply chain vulnerabilities. Policymakers must focus on refining dispute settlement processes and labor mechanisms to ensure the agreement remains a stable foundation for continental trade rather than a source of recurring uncertainty.

articles.title: USMCA Forward 2026 launch
articles.summary: The USMCA faces its first joint review in July 2026, a critical juncture for North American trade stability following recent U.S. tariff impositions and legal challenges to trade authorities. The Brookings 'USMCA Forward 2026' report emphasizes that the shifting political and economic landscape, marked by increased uncertainty, requires strategic priorities to ensure regional competitiveness. Ultimately, the policy choices made during this review will determine the resilience of North American supply chains and the future of economic security amidst global competition.

articles.title: United States-Mexico-Canada Agreement 2026: Review and déjà vu
articles.summary: The 2026 USMCA Forward report highlights a period of significant uncertainty as the agreement undergoes its first-ever joint review, with the U.S. currently signaling a preference for continuation without renewal unless key concessions are obtained. While trade and investment flows have grown under the agreement, the analysis points to strained diplomatic trust and sectoral challenges in automotive, steel, and agriculture due to persistent tariff threats. Ultimately, the review process serves as a critical mechanism for adapting the trade framework to modern economic realities, though its long-term stability depends on addressing U.S. demands for structural revisions.

articles.title: How can the USMCA support a more competitive North America?
articles.summary: The article argues that the USMCA serves as a vital framework for North American economic integration and a strategic asset against rising global geopolitical and economic uncertainty. It emphasizes that strengthening supply chain resilience in critical sectors like energy and high-tech is essential for maintaining the continent's competitive edge and addressing the challenges of non-market economic practices. The upcoming 2026 USMCA review presents a strategic opportunity to reaffirm the agreement's success while ensuring it remains responsive to technological disruption and economic security needs. To ensure long-term prosperity, the North American partners must prioritize a predictable regulatory environment and deeper cooperation in innovation-heavy industries.

articles.title: Reduced immigration slowed population growth for the nation and most states, new census data show
articles.summary: New Census Bureau data indicates that a sharp reduction in international migration has nearly halved U.S. population growth, which fell to 0.52% in the 2024-25 period. Stricter immigration policies and increased deportations led to a drop in net migration from 2.7 million to 1.3 million, causing 48 states to experience slower growth or absolute population declines. As natural population increase remains historically low due to an aging demographic, immigration now accounts for the vast majority of U.S. population gains. These findings suggest that continued migration restrictions will likely lead to widespread population stagnation and labor force shortages, threatening long-term economic productivity across nearly every state.

articles.title: ICE expansion has outpaced accountability. What are the remedies?
articles.summary: This report argues that the rapid expansion of ICE has severely outpaced accountability mechanisms, leading to systemic civil rights violations and the deaths of U.S. citizens. The authors cite a drastic reduction in agent training—from 22 weeks to 47 days—alongside lowered hiring standards and the pursuit of 'absolute immunity' as primary drivers of this crisis. The surge in enforcement has resulted in widespread reports of excessive force and racial profiling, undermining the legitimacy of federal law enforcement. To restore constitutional protections, the analysis recommends implementing mandatory body cameras, enhanced de-escalation training, and the removal of absolute immunity.

articles.title: What will 2026 bring for US migration policy?
articles.summary: The report contends that the current 'deterrence-only' immigration posture is counterproductive, citing its role in driving negative net migration and a $50 billion reduction in consumer spending. Key evidence highlights how aggressive enforcement without legal pathways has exacerbated labor shortages in critical sectors while failing to address the root causes of displacement. The analysis suggests that a sustainable strategy must integrate swift enforcement with expanded lawful pathways and regional cooperation to manage migration flows effectively. Ultimately, the choice for 2026 lies between maintaining a cycle of manufactured crises or implementing a modernized system that aligns with U.S. economic and security interests.

articles.title: Macroeconomic implications of immigration flows in 2025 and 2026: January 2026 update
articles.summary: Brookings estimates that U.S. net migration likely turned negative in 2025 for the first time in 50 years, with projections suggesting continued declines through 2026 due to restrictive policies and increased enforcement. This shift is driven by a sharp reduction in new arrivals—including green cards, refugees, and humanitarian parole—alongside a rise in both formal removals and voluntary departures. The resulting population pressure significantly lowers 'breakeven employment growth' to between 20,000 and 50,000 jobs per month and is expected to reduce consumer spending by up to $110 billion. Consequently, policymakers and the Federal Reserve must account for these structural labor supply constraints when interpreting weak employment data and setting monetary policy.

The resulting population pressure significantly lowers 'breakeven employment growth' to between 20,000 and 50,000 jobs per month and is expected to reduce consumer spending by up to $110 billion. Consequently, policymakers and the Federal Reserve must account for these structural labor supply constraints when interpreting weak employment data and setting monetary policy.

zh.summary: 布魯金斯學會（Brookings）估計，2025 年美國淨移民人數可能出現 50 年來首次負成長，且受限制性政策與加強執法影響，預計 2026 年將持續下滑。此轉變是由新入境人數（包括綠卡、難民與人道主義假釋）驟減，以及正式驅逐與自願離境人數增加所致。由此產生的人口壓力將「就業成長平衡點」顯著降低至每月 2 萬至 5 萬個工作職位，並預期減少高達 1,100 億美元的消費支出。因此，決策者與聯準會（Federal Reserve）在解讀疲軟的就業數據及制定貨幣政策時，必須考慮這些結構性勞動力供應限制。

articles.title: Tracking Trump’s tariffs and other trade actions
articles.summary: The Brookings Institution has launched a comprehensive tracker to monitor the significant expansion of U.S. tariffs implemented since January 2025, targeting major trading partners including Canada, Mexico, China, and the EU. These measures include broad sectoral tariffs on commodities like steel and aluminum, alongside country-specific adjustments tied to USMCA compliance and ongoing trade negotiations. By documenting trade-weighted tariff changes and retaliatory actions, the tracker highlights a pivot toward more protectionist U.S. trade policies. Continuous monitoring of these developments is critical for assessing the long-term impact on global economic stability and the status of evolving trade agreements.

zh.summary: 布魯金斯學會（Brookings Institution）啟動了一項全面的追蹤工具，旨在監測自 2025 年 1 月以來美國關稅政策的顯著擴張，其目標針對包括加拿大、墨西哥、中國及歐盟在內的主要貿易夥伴。這些措施包括對鋼鐵和鋁等大宗商品徵收廣泛的行業關稅，以及與《美墨加協定》（USMCA）合規性和進行中貿易談判相關的特定國家調整。藉由記錄貿易加權關稅變動及報復性行動，該追蹤器凸顯了美國貿易政策正朝向更強的保護主義轉向。持續監測這些進展對於評估其對全球經濟穩定及演變中貿易協定地位的長期影響至關重要。

articles.title: Four reasons Trump’s economic agenda hasn’t tanked the economy
articles.summary: The article examines why the U.S. economy has remained resilient with moderate growth and low unemployment despite unprecedented policy shocks, including high tariffs, negative net immigration, and massive debt expansion. The author attributes this stability to factors such as offsetting stimuli from the AI boom, potential overestimation of initial shock magnitudes, and the inherent time lag required for structural shifts to manifest. Ultimately, the piece warns that while the economy has absorbed these changes so far, the long-term erosion of institutional independence and global trade integration poses significant future risks.

zh.summary: 本文探討了儘管面臨高關稅、淨移民負成長及大規模債務擴張等前所未有的政策衝擊，美國經濟為何仍能保持韌性，維持溫和增長與低失業率。作者將此穩定性歸因於人工智慧（AI）熱潮帶來的抵銷性刺激、對初期衝擊規模的潛在過高估計，以及結構性轉變顯現所需的內在滯後時間。最後，文章警告稱，雖然經濟至今已吸收了這些變化，但制度獨立性的長期侵蝕和全球貿易整合的倒退，將對未來構成重大風險。

articles.title: Did ‘America First’ tariffs work?
articles.summary: This Brookings analysis concludes that while the 'America First' tariffs of 2025 did not trigger an immediate recession, they signify a definitive end to the post-WWII rules-based liberal trade order. Despite the resilience of the U.S. economy, the tariffs have contributed to persistent inflation and restricted long-term growth by limiting competition and access to global value chains. The shift toward using trade as a tool for foreign policy objectives, particularly to counter Chinese manufacturing dominance, marks a transition to a 'non-adversarial reliance' model that prioritizes national security over market efficiency. This new era of economic statecraft suggests that while the U.S. has avoided short-term shocks, the long-term consequences may manifest in slower productivity growth and strained international alliances.

zh.summary: 這份布魯金斯學會（Brookings）的分析報告總結道，儘管 2025 年的「美國優先」關稅並未立即引發經濟衰退，但它們標誌著二戰後基於規則的自由貿易秩序已徹底終結。儘管美國經濟具有韌性，但關稅透過限制競爭和進入全球價值鏈的管道，導致了持續的通膨並限制了長期增長。將貿易轉向作為外交政策目標的工具，特別是為了抗衡中國的製造業優勢，標誌著向「非對抗性依賴」模式的轉變，該模式優先考慮國家安全而非市場效率。這一經濟治理的新時代顯示，雖然美國避開了短期衝擊，但長期後果可能體現為生產力增長放緩以及國際盟友關係緊張。

articles.title: What incentives are states offering to make houses less vulnerable to extreme weather damage?
articles.summary: Various U.S. states are increasingly offering grants and loans to incentivize homeowners to retrofit properties against extreme weather risks like hurricanes, wildfires, and floods. Evidence from established programs in Alabama and Florida indicates that adhering to resilience standards like 'FORTIFIED Home' can reduce storm damage by up to 75% and increase property resale values by approximately 7%. These initiatives suggest a shift toward proactive disaster mitigation as a strategy to stabilize volatile insurance markets and lower long-term disaster recovery costs. However, the effectiveness of these policies remains contingent on consistent multi-year funding and overcoming administrative barriers to homeowner participation.

zh.summary: 美國各州正日益增加提供補助金與貸款，以激勵屋主針對颶風、野火和洪水等極端天氣風險進行房屋抗災加固。來自阿拉巴馬州和佛羅里達州既有計畫的證據顯示，遵循如「FORTIFIED Home」等韌性標準，最高可減少 75% 的風暴損害，並使物業轉售價值提高約 7%。這些舉措顯示，政策正轉向主動減災，以此作為穩定波動的保險市場並降低長期災後復原成本的策略。然而，這些政策的成效仍取決於持續多年的資金挹注，以及能否克服屋主參與時面臨的行政障礙。

articles.title: Who we count shapes how we measure housing supply and affordability
articles.summary: Current housing supply and affordability metrics rely heavily on 'household heads,' a framework that masks the actual housing strain experienced by nearly half of the adult population who are not designated as heads. Analysis of 2024 American Community Survey data reveals that non-head adults often differ significantly from heads in age and education, with younger individuals being much more exposed to high housing costs than head-based statistics suggest. These measurement gaps risk underestimating true housing demand and mistargeting relief policies, as suppressed headship rates often reflect economic constraints rather than a genuine reduction in housing need.

zh.summary: 目前的房屋供應與負擔能力指標過度依賴「戶主」框架，這掩蓋了近半數非戶主成年人口所承受的真實住房壓力。對 2024 年美國社區調查數據的分析顯示，非戶主成年人在年齡與教育程度上通常與戶主有顯著差異，且年輕族群面臨高昂住房成本的程度遠高於以戶主為基礎的統計數據所呈現的情況。這些衡量落差可能導致低估真實住房需求，並使紓困政策失去精準度，因為受抑制的戶主率往往反映的是經濟限制，而非住房需求的真實減少。

articles.title: Helping low-income families access WIC and free early childhood education
articles.summary: A randomized controlled trial in Louisiana demonstrates that reducing administrative burdens by providing information and data-sharing support can increase WIC application rates by approximately 30%. While streamlining the initial application process effectively lowers learning costs, the study found that enrollment gains were more limited because families still face significant obstacles in subsequent steps, such as in-person interviews. These findings suggest that while digital integration is a valuable first step, policymakers must address the entire lifecycle of benefit enrollment and maintain human-centric support to successfully reach marginalized populations.

zh.summary: 路易斯安那州的一項隨機對照試驗顯示，透過提供資訊與數據共享支援來減輕行政負擔，可使 WIC（婦幼營養補助計劃）的申請率提高約 30%。儘管精簡初步申請流程能有效降低學習成本，但研究發現，由於家庭在面談等後續步驟中仍面臨重大障礙，入榜人數的增長受到限制。這些結果顯示，數位整合雖是極具價值的初步步驟，但政策制定者必須關注福利登記的全生命週期，並維持以人為本的支援系統，方能成功觸及邊緣化群體。

articles.title: Tracking the labor market and jobs
articles.summary: Brookings has updated its interactive 'Tracking the labor market and jobs' tool, which utilizes harmonized Current Population Survey data to provide a comprehensive view of the U.S. labor market. The platform allows users to analyze trends in labor force participation, employment ratios, and unemployment metrics across diverse demographic categories such as nativity, disability status, and educational attainment. By offering granular, seasonal adjustments and cross-tabulated data, the tool enables a deeper understanding of how economic shifts uniquely impact specific population segments. This resource is essential for policymakers seeking to design targeted interventions and monitor the effectiveness of economic strategies in real-time.

articles.title: AI + work: Understanding AI’s impact on the labor market
AI, workers, and national security in a changing world: A conversation with Sen. Mark Kelly
articles.summary: Senator Mark Kelly’s 'AI for America' roadmap advocates for integrated policies to support workers and expand domestic infrastructure to meet the computational demands of artificial intelligence. The strategy addresses critical constraints in energy, capital, and skilled labor while navigating the technology's profound implications for military capability and geopolitical competition. By proposing legislative measures for AI literacy and resource management, the roadmap seeks to balance productivity gains with the need to mitigate localized economic disruption and maintain national security. These policy choices will determine the pace of AI adoption and its role in reshaping the global balance of power.

articles.title: From evidence to action: How cities are investing in playful learning landscapes
articles.summary: The Brookings Center for Universal Education’s 'Playful Learning Landscapes' (PLL) initiative advocates for transforming everyday urban spaces into engaging learning environments to improve early childhood outcomes. By integrating educational elements into locations like bus stops and parks, the initiative leverages the significant portion of children's learning that occurs outside traditional classrooms. The successful implementation of these evidence-based strategies in cities like Philadelphia and Santa Ana demonstrates how urban policy can be reshaped to foster child development and strengthen family well-being.

zh.summary: 布魯金斯學會全球教育中心的「寓教於樂地景」（Playful Learning Landscapes, PLL）倡議，主張將日常城市空間轉化為具吸引力的學習環境，以提升幼兒發展成效。透過在公車站和公園等場所融入教育元素，該倡議充分利用了兒童在傳統教室外的大部分學習機會。在費城和聖安娜等城市的成功實施經驗，展示了城市政策如何經由重塑來促進兒童發展並增進家庭福祉。

articles.title: The Geopolitics of Russia’s Civil Nuclear Exports Four Years into the War
articles.summary: Four years into the Ukraine conflict, Russia's global nuclear influence remains resilient in the Global South despite Western decoupling and significant sanction-induced financial hurdles. While projects in countries like Turkey and Bangladesh continue through alternative payment systems and logistical workarounds, Rosatom's new business prospects are increasingly limited to the Arctic and CIS states. The report suggests that Russia's long-term dominance is fading as economic strain and the emergence of China as a viable technological competitor provide partners with alternatives. Strategic implications include the need for Western nations to bolster domestic fuel cycles and monitor the deepening Sino-Russian nuclear partnership in emerging markets.

articles.title: The Satellite Encryption Gap: Why Everyday Citizens’ Communications Are at Risk
articles.summary: CSIS warns that a critical 'encryption gap' in commercial satellite constellations leaves global digital infrastructure vulnerable to low-cost interception by adversaries. A 2025 academic study demonstrated that $800 off-the-shelf equipment could capture sensitive data, including military movements and private civilian communications, from unencrypted satellite links. To mitigate risks from nation-states like China and Russia, the authors recommend mandating 'secure-by-design' encryption standards for commercial providers and leveraging federal procurement to drive industry-wide adoption.

To mitigate risks from nation-states like China and Russia, the authors recommend mandating 'secure-by-design' encryption standards for commercial providers and leveraging federal procurement to drive industry-wide adoption.

zh.summary: CSIS 警告，商用衛星群中關鍵的「加密缺口」使全球數位基礎設施面臨遭敵對勢力低成本攔截的風險。2025 年的一項學術研究顯示，僅需 800 美元的現成設備，即可從未加密的衛星鏈路中擷取敏感數據，包括軍事行動及私人平民通訊。為應對來自中國與俄羅斯等國家的風險，作者建議強制要求商用供應商採納「安全設計」（secure-by-design）加密標準，並透過聯邦採購機制推動產業全面轉型。

articles.title: No One, Not Even Beijing, Is Getting Through the Strait of Hormuz
articles.summary: Following US-Israel strikes on Iran, maritime traffic through the Strait of Hormuz has collapsed, with Chinese vessels failing to secure safe passage despite Beijing’s diplomatic ties with Tehran. Ship-tracking data shows Chinese transits have plummeted to near zero, leaving 55 ships trapped and highlighting China’s significant vulnerability to regional instability and energy disruptions. This divergence in strategic priorities between Iran’s regime survival and China’s energy needs suggests that Beijing may eventually be forced to shift from passive calls for restraint to active pressure on combatants. Ultimately, the crisis underscores the limits of China’s influence in the Middle East when faced with high-intensity kinetic conflict.

articles.title: What Does the Iran War Mean for Global Energy Markets?
articles.summary: The sudden conflict in the Persian Gulf has significantly disrupted global energy security, causing oil prices to surge and halting critical LNG exports through the Strait of Hormuz. While robust U.S. shale production and healthy strategic reserves mitigate a total price collapse, the destruction of infrastructure and force majeure declarations in Qatar have removed millions of barrels from daily global supply. Consequently, the crisis is likely to accelerate a global shift toward energy diversification and increase the strategic appeal of U.S. LNG as a more stable alternative to Middle Eastern sources.

While robust U.S. shale production and healthy strategic reserves mitigate a total price collapse, the destruction of infrastructure and force majeure declarations in Qatar have removed millions of barrels from daily global supply. Consequently, the crisis is likely to accelerate a global shift toward energy diversification and increase the strategic appeal of U.S. LNG as a more stable alternative to Middle Eastern sources.

zh.summary: 波斯灣突發的衝突嚴重衝擊全球能源安全，造成國際油價飆升，並阻斷了經由荷姆茲海峽的關鍵液化天然氣（LNG）出口。雖然美國強韌的頁岩油產量與充足的戰略儲備防止了價格體系的全面崩潰，但卡達境內的基礎設施損毀及不可抗力聲明，已導致全球每日供應減少數百萬桶。因此，此場危機預期將加速全球能源多元化的轉型趨勢，並強化美國液化天然氣作為中東能源更穩定替代選項的戰略地位。

articles.title: Russian Crude and India: Here to Stay Amid Middle East Tensions?
articles.summary: India is likely to maintain its reliance on Russian crude oil despite U.S. pressure, as escalating Middle East tensions and the blockade of the Strait of Hormuz threaten traditional Gulf supplies. While India had previously reduced Russian imports to roughly 20%, a recent 24% price spike and threats to over half of its energy source have forced a return to pragmatic procurement. Consequently, the U.S. has issued waivers to prevent an Indian economic crisis, illustrating how energy security concerns are currently outweighing the strategic goal of isolating Russia’s war chest. This shift indicates that Russian oil will remain a vital, chokepoint-proof alternative for India during periods of regional instability.

zh.summary: 儘管面臨美國的壓力，印度仍可能維持對俄羅斯原油的依賴，因為中東緊張局勢升級和荷姆茲海峽的封鎖威脅到傳統的海灣供應。雖然印度此前已將俄羅斯進口比例降至約 20%，但近期 24% 的價格飆升以及對其一半以上能源來源的威脅，迫使其回歸務實採購。因此，美國已發放豁免以防止印度發生經濟危機，這說明了能源安全考量目前已超過了孤立俄羅斯戰爭資金的戰略目標。這一轉變表明，在地區不穩定期間，俄羅斯石油仍將是印度至關重要且能避開咽喉點的替代方案。

articles.title: Risk Beneath the Waves: Safeguarding Subsea Cables for a Secure Global Network
From Compliance to Strategy: Rethinking the Role of Human Rights in National Security and Countering Violent Extremism
articles.summary: This CSIS analysis argues that Countering Violent Extremism (CVE) frameworks must shift from viewing human rights as a mere legal compliance requirement to a strategic asset for national security. Using examples from Afghanistan, Nigeria, and Somalia, the author demonstrates how 'security-first' approaches that disregard human rights often backfire by fueling local grievances and aiding extremist recruitment. To ensure sustainable security, the article recommends that national and international bodies integrate human rights-centric strategies, robust monitoring offices, and conditional support based on adherence to international law.

zh.summary: 這份 CSIS 分析主張，對抗暴力極端主義 (CVE) 的框架必須進行轉型，將人權從單純的法律合規要求提升為國家安全的戰略資產。作者透過阿富汗、奈及利亞與索馬利亞的案例，揭示了忽視人權的「安全至上」做法，往往會因激起地方民怨並助長極端組織招募而適得其反。為確保永續的安全，本文建議各國與國際機構應整合以人權為核心的戰略，建立完善的監測機制，並根據對國際法的遵守情況提供有條件的支援。

articles.title: The Shield of Americas Gathering and an Amplified Strategy to Counter China in the Western Hemisphere
articles.summary: The CSIS report argues that the 'Shield of the Americas' gathering provides a pivotal platform for the Trump administration to execute a comprehensive strategy to counter Chinese influence in the Western Hemisphere. The author highlights China's extensive control over regional strategic assets, including a 36-port network and deep telecommunications penetration, as a primary threat to U.S. interests. To address this, the administration proposes a suite of initiatives—such as a $50-100 billion infrastructure compact and 'rip and replace' programs for digital networks—designed to offer U.S.-backed alternatives to Beijing’s Belt and Road Initiative. Ultimately, these efforts seek to institutionalize a 'Trump Corollary to the Monroe Doctrine' by requiring regional partners to adopt stricter transparency and security standards to maintain alignment with Washington.

zh.summary: 戰略與國際研究中心（CSIS）的報告指出，「美洲之盾」（Shield of the Americas）集會為川普政府執行應對中國在西半球影響力的全面戰略提供了關鍵平台。作者強調，中國對區域戰略資產的廣泛控制——包括由 36 個港口組成的網絡以及深度的電信滲透——是對美國利益的主要威脅。為此，川普政府提出了一系列倡議，如價值 500 億至 1000 億美元的基礎設施協議，以及針對數位網絡的「拆除與更換」（rip and replace）計畫，旨在提供由美國支持的方案，以取代北京的「一帶一路」倡議。最終，這些努力尋求透過要求區域夥伴採用更嚴格的透明度與安全標準來維持與華盛頓的一致性，進而將「門羅主義的川普推論」制度化。

articles.title: $3.7 Billion: Estimated Cost of Epic Fury’s First 100 Hours
articles.summary: CSIS estimates that the first 100 hours of Operation Epic Fury against Iran cost approximately $3.7 billion, of which $3.5 billion is currently unbudgeted. These high initial costs were driven primarily by $3.1 billion in munitions expenditures, including expensive standoff missiles and air defense interceptors used to secure air superiority. While costs are expected to trend downward as the military transitions to cheaper 'stand-in' munitions and leverages regional allied support, the funding gap will likely require a contentious supplemental defense appropriation from Congress.

zh.summary: CSIS 估計，針對伊朗的「史詩之怒」行動（Operation Epic Fury）在最初 100 小時內的成本約為 37 億美元，其中 35 億美元目前尚未列入預算。這些高昂的初始成本主要源於 31 億美元的彈藥支出，包括為確保制空權而使用的昂貴防區外飛彈與防空攔截彈。雖然隨著軍方轉向使用較廉價的「介入型」彈藥並善用區域盟友的支持，預計成本將呈下降趨勢，但資金缺口可能仍需國會通過一項具爭議性的補充國防撥款。

articles.title: Epic Fury: The Campaign Against Iran’s Missile & Nuclear Infrastructure
articles.summary: This CSIS analysis evaluates the initial phase of 'Operation Epic Fury,' a joint U.S.-Israeli preventive campaign aimed at the comprehensive destruction of Iran's missile, nuclear, and naval infrastructure. Experts highlight that the operation addresses a strategic imbalance where Iran’s missile production rates outpaced U.S. interceptor inventories, while also noting early successes in neutralizing Iranian leadership and degrading retaliatory capabilities. Strategic implications include an urgent requirement for a triple-digit billion-dollar munitions supplemental to replenish global stockpiles and the potential necessity of ground forces for verification and nuclear material security.

articles.title: Preventing Renewed Conflict in Colombia
articles.summary: The report argues that the United States must proactively engage with Colombia's incoming 2026 administration to ensure the full implementation of the 2016 Peace Accords and prevent a return to widespread civil conflict. Evidence suggests that worsening internal violence, the expansion of armed groups, and slow progress on reintegration guarantees have pushed the peace process to a breaking point, compounded by regional spillover from Venezuela. To protect national security interests and stabilize the region, the U.S. should prioritize a bilateral reset that emphasizes diplomatic accompaniment, innovative financial support through international institutions, and targeted security assistance rather than direct military intervention.

zh.summary: 該報告指出，美國必須積極與哥倫比亞 2026 年即將上任的政府接觸，以確保 2016 年和平協議得到全面履行，並防止重返大規模內戰。證據顯示，內部暴力加劇、武裝團體擴張以及重新融入保障進展緩慢，已將和平進程推向崩潰邊緣，而委內瑞拉的區域溢出效應更使局勢雪上加霜。為維護國家安全利益並穩定該地區，美國應優先考慮雙邊關係的重啟，重點在於外交陪同、透過國際機構提供創新財務支持以及有針對性的安全援助，而非直接軍事干預。

articles.title: Leapfrogging China’s Critical Minerals Dominance
articles.summary: The report argues that the United States cannot out-mine China and must instead "leapfrog" its dominance by scaling disruptive innovations in materials science, waste recovery, and recycling. Analysts emphasize that while traditional mining takes decades to mature, U.S. strengths in AI-enabled research and bio-engineered extraction can bypass Chinese choke points such as heavy rare-earth magnets. To succeed, the authors recommend a national innovation strategy centered on bridging commercialization financing gaps and coordinating with G7 allies to build a circular, independent mineral supply chain.

zh.summary: 該報告指出，美國無法在採礦產量上與中國競爭，必須轉而透過擴大材料科學、廢物回收與再利用領域的破壞性創新，來實現對中國主導地位的「跨越式」突破。分析人士強調，雖然傳統採礦業需要數十年才能成熟，但美國在人工智慧輔助研究與生物工程提取技術方面的優勢，能繞過如重稀土磁鐵等中國的「鎖喉」制約。為此，作者建議制定一項國家創新戰略，重點在於填補商業化融資缺口，並與 G7 盟友合作，構建一個循環且自主的礦產供應鏈。

articles.title: America Revived
articles.summary: Robert D. Blackwill proposes a grand strategy of 'resolute global leadership' as the optimal path for the United States to counter a peer-competitor China and manage the most dangerous international environment since World War II. The strategy synthesizes military superiority with revitalized international cooperation, arguing that American structural advantages—such as its global alliance network and innovation lead—outperform isolationist or purely transactional alternatives. To succeed, the report recommends increasing defense spending, pivoting military assets to Asia, and reversing protectionist trade policies to restore U.S. legitimacy and economic strength. Ultimately, this approach seeks to balance Chinese power through 'peace through strength' while maintaining the stability of the global rules-based order.

articles.title: Conflicts to Watch in 2026
articles.summary: The 2026 Preventive Priorities Survey identifies 30 global conflicts posing significant risks to U.S. national security, highlighting five high-likelihood, high-impact threats including intensified wars in Ukraine and Gaza, potential U.S. military action in Venezuela, and domestic political unrest. The report notes a dangerous shift toward interstate conflict and warns that the dismantling of U.S. conflict-prevention infrastructure increases the likelihood of being blindsided by crises. Experts argue that while risks of great power war persist, the U.S. retains critical leverage to mitigate conflict in Ukraine and the Middle East through proactive diplomacy. Ultimately, the findings urge a strategic return to 'upstream' conflict prevention to protect U.S. interests in an increasingly disorderly world.

zh.summary: 《2026年預防優先事項調查》辨識出30個對美國國家安全構成重大風險的全球衝突，並強調了五項高可能性、高衝擊的威脅，包括烏克蘭與加薩日益加劇的戰爭、美國在委內瑞拉採取軍事行動的可能性，以及國內政治動盪。報告指出，當前局勢正向國家間衝突危險轉向，並警告美國衝突預防機制的瓦解，增加了在危機中措手不及的可能性。專家認為，儘管大國戰爭的風險依然存在，但美國仍保有關鍵影響力，能透過主動外交緩解烏克蘭與中東的衝突。最終，研究結果敦促策略性地回歸「上游」衝突預防，以在日益混亂的世界中保護美國利益。

articles.title: Compete, Don’t Retreat
articles.summary: The report argues that the United States must shift from a purely protectionist stance to a proactive strategy of competing with China in the autonomous, connected, and electric (ACE) vehicle market. It contends that while current tariffs provide temporary breathing room, indefinite isolation risks leaving the U.S. auto industry technologically obsolete and uncompetitive as the global market shifts toward Chinese-led innovations. To maintain leadership, the U.S. should provide conditional financial support for domestic repositioning, collaborate with allies on supply chain diversification, and implement rigorous data localization standards for imported technologies.

zh.summary: 該報告主張美國必須從純粹的保護主義立場，轉向在自動駕駛、聯網及電動 (ACE) 車輛市場中與中國競爭的主動策略。報告認為，雖然目前的關稅提供了暫時的喘息空間，但隨著全球市場轉向由中國主導的創新，無限期的孤立可能導致美國汽車工業在技術上過時並失去競爭力。為了維持領導地位，美國應為國內產業轉型提供有條件的財政支持，與盟友合作實現供應鏈多元化，並對進口技術實施嚴格的數據在地化標準。

articles.title: The Next Taiwan Crisis Won’t Be Like the Last
articles.summary: The report argues that future conflicts over Taiwan will likely escalate into geographically expansive, multi-actor regional wars, rendering outdated the traditional 'three-party' containment model. Evidence suggests that China’s military modernization and the strategic necessity of Japanese and Philippine bases make preemptive strikes and cross-theater spillover from the South China Sea or Korean Peninsula highly probable. To address these risks, U.S. policymakers should establish multilateral pre-crisis consultative mechanisms with Indo-Pacific allies and accelerate the integration of joint military command structures. This shift is essential for managing simultaneous contingencies and ensuring operational warning in an increasingly unstable global security environment.

articles.title: What’s Next for the War in Iran?
articles.summary: The ongoing U.S. and Israeli military campaign in Iran has significantly degraded the regime's power and eliminated its top leadership, yet the operation's ultimate success hinges on the uncertain prospects of a stable political transition. While key objectives focus on dismantling Iran’s nuclear and missile programs, the conflict has already severely disrupted global energy markets through the near-total halt of tanker traffic in the Strait of Hormuz. Policymakers now face a complex succession landscape involving competing clerical and military factions, where the failure to secure a more peaceful regime could result in a prolonged regional quagmire. Additionally, the war serves as a critical testing ground for innovative defense technologies, such as interceptor drones and directed energy weapons, to counter asymmetric threats.

zh.summary: 美國與以色列目前在伊朗進行的軍事行動已顯著削弱該政權實力並清除了其高層領導，然而行動的最終成功仍取決於政治過渡是否穩定這一不確定前景。雖然核心目標聚焦於拆除伊朗的核能與飛彈計畫，但衝突已因荷姆茲海峽油輪運輸幾近停擺，對全球能源市場造成嚴重衝擊。決策者目前面臨涉及教士與軍事派系競爭的複雜權力繼承格局，若無法確保建立更和平的政權，恐將陷入長期的區域泥淖。此外，這場戰爭亦成為測試攔截無人機與定向能武器等創新國防技術，以應對不對稱威脅的關鍵試驗場。

articles.title: Europe’s Disjointed Response to the War With Iran
articles.summary: European leaders have responded in a fragmented manner to the uncoordinated U.S.-Israeli military strikes on Iran, revealing deep internal divisions regarding the use of force and international law. While countries like Poland and Germany offer political or conditional support, France and Southern European nations have voiced legal criticisms, highlighting a lack of unified strategic weight. The conflict underscores Europe's continued dependence on the United States even as it pursues greater autonomy through increased defense spending and independent financial support for Ukraine. Ultimately, the war in the Middle East threatens to distract Washington from the European theater and disrupt energy markets, further straining the transatlantic relationship.

articles.title: Can the Kurds Challenge the Iranian Regime?
articles.summary: Following joint U.S.-Israeli strikes on Tehran, Iranian Kurdish groups are reportedly mobilizing with potential U.S. support, though their capacity to successfully mount an armed resistance remains doubtful in the short term. Despite the formation of a united political front, these groups lack the combat experience of their regional counterparts and face significant logistical hurdles, including long training timelines and opposition from local Iraqi authorities. The success of any Kurdish uprising hinges on sustained international backing, yet historical precedents and regional interference from powers like Turkey suggest a high risk of instability. Ultimately, while a weakened regime might offer Kurds some autonomy, policy analysts warn that externally induced change could trigger sectarian conflict similar to post-2003 Iraq.

articles.title: Congress Declines to Demand a Say in the Iran War
articles.summary: Congress has effectively abdicated its constitutional war-making authority by failing to pass resolutions requiring presidential authorization for military operations against Iran. Lawmakers largely favored executive flexibility during active conflict, with the House and Senate votes reflecting deep partisan divisions rather than a unified defense of legislative oversight. This outcome suggests that the executive branch will continue to exercise broad discretion in initiating hostilities, as the courts historically avoid such political questions. Moving forward, any legislative check on the conflict will likely depend on the difficult-to-wield power of the purse or a significant escalation involving ground forces.

articles.title: U.S. Homeland Security Concerns After Iran Strikes
articles.summary: The ongoing conflict with Iran significantly raises the risk of asymmetric retaliation against the U.S. homeland, encompassing lone-wolf terrorism, cyberattacks, and strikes on critical infrastructure. Historically, Tehran has utilized sleeper agents and criminal proxies for state-sponsored terrorism, suggesting that revenge for recent strikes may be deferred until high-profile events like the World Cup. However, U.S. defensive capabilities are currently strained by the Department of Homeland Security's shift toward immigration enforcement and significant workforce cuts in specialized counterintelligence units. Consequently, experts urge an immediate re-prioritization of counterterrorism resources to address these evolving unconventional security threats.

articles.title: U.S. Campaign in Iran Ignores Iraq War Lessons
articles.summary: The article contends that the Trump administration's current military operations against Iran repeat the strategic errors of the Iraq War by failing to establish a clear post-conflict stabilization plan. Drawing on historical comparisons, the author notes that relying on a solo air campaign ignores the resilience of the IRGC and the high probability of unpredictable regional upheaval. The piece warns that without a diplomatic framework or a realistic 'Phase IV' strategy, the U.S. faces the prospect of a fragmented Iran and a protracted crisis that will ultimately damage American interests regardless of the administration's desire to avoid responsibility.

This escalation underscores a shift toward military force to prevent a nuclear-armed Iran, though it has yet to fully dismantle the program's technical foundations. The ongoing conflict risks a broader regional war and may incentivize neighboring states like Saudi Arabia to pursue their own nuclear capabilities.

articles.title: U.S. Relations With Iran
articles.summary: This CFR report outlines the catastrophic collapse of U.S.-Iran relations, culminating in a massive joint U.S.-Israeli military campaign in February 2026. Following failed nuclear talks and the failure of 'maximum pressure' sanctions, the conflict escalated to direct strikes that killed Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei and targeted Iran's nuclear and naval assets. These events have triggered immediate regional retaliation, including Iranian strikes on U.S. Gulf bases and the closure of the Strait of Hormuz, presenting a severe threat to global energy stability and risking a broader regional war.

articles.title: The Islamic Republic of Iran’s Power Centers
articles.summary: Following the killing of Supreme Leader Khamenei and devastating U.S.-Israeli military strikes in early 2026, Iran’s complex governance structure faces an unprecedented succession crisis and existential instability. The report explains that an interim three-person council is currently managing the state while the Assembly of Experts searches for a successor amidst a backdrop of domestic unrest and military degradation. Despite these pressures, the regime’s ideological elite and the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps maintain the capacity to use force to preserve the existing system. Consequently, the transition represents a critical inflection point that could either destabilize the Middle East further or lead to a significant reconfiguration of Iranian power.

articles.title: The Strait of Hormuz: A U.S.-Iran Maritime Flash Point
articles.summary: The joint U.S.-Israeli strikes against Iran and the subsequent death of Supreme Leader Khamenei have turned the Strait of Hormuz into a volatile maritime flashpoint, severely threatening global energy markets. In response to Iranian retaliation and threats of a blockade, vessel traffic through the waterway has dropped by 70%, causing Brent crude and natural gas prices to surge. While U.S. military operations have significantly degraded Iran's formal naval capacity, the continued use of asymmetric tactics like drone strikes and mine-laying forces expensive shipping diversions. This escalation highlights the fragility of regional maritime security and the immediate risk of a broader conflict disrupting essential global trade routes.

articles.title: What Is Hezbollah?
articles.summary: Hezbollah remains a critical Iranian proxy in Lebanon, although its military capacity and leadership were significantly degraded by Israeli campaigns in 2024. The group's 2024 ceasefire with Israel collapsed in February 2026 after Hezbollah launched retaliatory strikes following the killing of Iranian Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei during a joint U.S.-Israeli military operation. While weakened, Hezbollah continues to function as a 'state within a state,' utilizing its remaining arsenal and social service networks to maintain influence amidst expanding regional hostilities. The current escalation signals a dangerous transition into a broader direct conflict between the U.S.-Israel alliance and Iran's regional network, posing severe risks to Lebanese and Middle Eastern stability.

articles.summary: The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) has consolidated its position as Iran's dominant military, political, and economic force, serving as the primary architect of regional proxy wars and domestic repression. Recent brutal crackdowns on 2026 protesters have triggered new international terrorist designations, while the group continues to leverage a multi-billion dollar shadow economy to fund its 'axis of resistance' and nuclear ambitions. The IRGC's entrenched influence suggests that future leadership succession will likely prioritize hard-line stability over reform, complicating Western efforts at regional de-escalation.

articles.title: Strait-jacket: Global Energy Flows and the War with Iran
articles.summary: The military conflict between the United States, Israel, and Iran has severely disrupted energy flows through the Strait of Hormuz, threatening twenty percent of global oil and gas supplies and disproportionately impacting Asian economies. While nations like Japan are buffered by significant strategic reserves, others like India face immediate risks due to limited storage and recent shifts in import patterns. Ultimately, these supply shocks are expected to drive a temporary resurgence in coal usage for affordability while simultaneously accelerating long-term strategic investments in nuclear and renewable energy to ensure national security and reduce reliance on volatile Middle Eastern transit routes.

articles.title: Americans Are Skeptical About Operation Epic Fury
articles.summary: Recent polling data indicates that the American public is largely skeptical of President Trump's decision to launch "Operation Epic Fury" against Iran, with several major surveys showing more disapproval than support. Evidence from Morning Consult, YouGov, and Reuters/Ipsos highlights a lack of a "rally-round-the-flag" effect and a persistent partisan divide in opinion. These findings suggest that the administration possesses limited political capital to sustain the conflict if it encounters military setbacks or triggers significant economic consequences, such as higher gasoline prices. Consequently, while immediate military operations may continue, the long-term sustainability of the policy depends heavily on avoiding adverse domestic impacts.

articles.title: Gauging the Impact of U.S.-Israeli Strikes on Iran
articles.summary: CFR experts assess the implications of 'Operation Epic Fury,' a joint U.S.-Israeli military campaign initiated on February 28, 2026, which killed Supreme Leader Khamenei but has yet to achieve its stated goal of regime change. The analysis emphasizes that air power alone is unlikely to dismantle the deeply entrenched Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) or permanently eliminate Iran’s proxy and missile capabilities. This tactical shift toward explicit regime change risks triggering a prolonged regional escalatory cycle, leaving Gulf allies vulnerable to Iranian reprisals and potentially necessitating a more costly ground intervention.

articles.title: The AI Sovereignty Paradox at Home and Abroad
articles.summary: The "AI sovereignty paradox" is defined by the tension between the U.S. government’s demand for unfettered military access to AI and the ethical safeguards maintained by private developers. This conflict, highlighted by the Pentagon’s recent standoff with Anthropic, illustrates the lack of a clear domestic regulatory framework for dual-use technologies. Internationally, middle powers are seeking digital sovereignty through localized regulations and infrastructure to reduce dependency on the dominant U.S.-Chinese "AI stack." Consequently, policymakers face the dual challenge of reconciling national security requirements with private sector safety standards while navigating a fragmented global regulatory landscape.

articles.title: The AI Bubble + The Productivity Paradox + India’s AI Summit
articles.summary: This analysis posits that while AI is a transformative "A+" technology, firms like OpenAI face an "F-" business model with a high risk of a financing cliff due to astronomical capital requirements and projected losses of $660 billion by 2030. Market fragility is evidenced by the "SaaS-pocalypse" and the potential for a "jobless expansion" as firms freeze hiring while awaiting productivity gains that have yet to appear in macroeconomic data. Consequently, the authors suggest resolving the "AI trilemma" by implementing a safety tax to fund independent research and empowering a national safety institute with veto authority over high-risk models to prevent societal and geopolitical disruption.

articles.title: Military AI Adoption Is Outpacing Global Cooperation
articles.summary: Global military AI adoption is rapidly outstripping international efforts to establish governance, as evidenced by a significant decline in endorsements at the recent REAIM summit. With the United States and China increasingly detached from multilateral dialogues, middle powers now face the critical choice of leading the development of 'rules of the road' or allowing the technology to evolve without international guardrails. The divergence between diplomatic negotiations and the real-world deployment of AI in ongoing conflicts risks making future policy efforts irrelevant to technical and battlefield realities.

articles.title: Why Trust Infrastructure Is the United States’ AI Advantage
articles.summary: The article argues that the United States' primary competitive advantage in AI lies in developing 'trust infrastructure'—credible assurance frameworks like independent validation and incident reporting—which enables confident large-scale deployment. By drawing on historical precedents in aviation and finance, the author posits that these mechanisms turn technical risks into manageable market assets, allowing the US to set global standards that allies can trust. Strategic implications suggest that the US must establish an integrated framework involving independent benchmarking and federal incident repositories within the next three years to prevent global market fragmentation. Establishing this infrastructure will ensure that American AI remains the global benchmark for high-stakes applications in health, finance, and national security.

articles.title: A Conversation With Elbridge Colby
articles.summary: Under Secretary Elbridge Colby outlines a National Defense Strategy rooted in 'flexible realism,' prioritizing the Western Hemisphere and homeland security while seeking a 'decent peace' in the Indo-Pacific through a balance of power. The strategy emphasizes a 'NATO 3.0' framework where allies take primary responsibility for conventional defense, supported by a 'national mobilization' of the U.S. defense industrial base to address munitions depletion and readiness. Recent operations against Iran and in Venezuela demonstrate a proactive, results-oriented approach to degrading threats and enforcing regional stability through burden-sharing with 'model allies.' This shift signifies a pivot toward pragmatic, interest-based military engagement that preserves U.S. high-end capabilities for essential deterrence.

articles.title: Media Briefing: What Comes Next After the U.S. and Israeli Strikes on Iran
articles.summary: CFR experts analyze the aftermath of unprecedented U.S.-Israeli strikes on Iran, which effectively neutralized its nuclear and missile infrastructure while causing the death of Supreme Leader Khamenei. Although tactically successful, the briefing underscores a lack of strategic clarity regarding the ultimate objective, oscillating between absolute regime change and a negotiated settlement with a weakened leadership. The discussion warns that while Iran's ability to project conventional force is decimated, the risk of asymmetric retaliation remains high, and the internal power vacuum could lead to either a hardline military takeover or state collapse.

articles.title: A Conversation With EXIM Bank President John Jovanovic
articles.summary: EXIM Bank President John Jovanovic outlines the agency's transformation into a cornerstone of U.S. economic statecraft, centered on the newly launched "Project Vault," a $12 billion strategic reserve for critical minerals. This initiative employs a public-private partnership to warehouse essential materials, aiming to derisk manufacturing supply chains from Chinese control while neutralizing price volatility for domestic producers. The shift reflects a broader strategy of assertive industrial policy that prioritizes energy dominance, AI leadership, and "friendshoring" with allies to ensure long-term U.S. competitiveness and resource security.

articles.title: Robert B. Menschel Economics Symposium: Lessons From 1929
articles.summary: The symposium concludes that the current AI investment boom exhibits classic bubble characteristics, with massive capital expenditures by tech giants significantly outpacing actual revenue generation. Panelists argue that while an AI market correction would primarily impact the corporate sector rather than the banking core, the combination of record-high federal debt and protectionist trade policies creates a 'red line' risk that could turn a market dip into a broader recession. To mitigate these risks, experts recommend proactive financial regulation and strengthening social safety nets, warning that policy errors—similar to those made following the 1929 crash—pose a greater threat than the market volatility itself.

articles.summary: The conflict in the Middle East has reached a volatile inflection point as Israel escalates its military offensive against Hezbollah in Beirut following the recent death of Iranian Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei. Despite significant degradation of Iranian missile launch sites by U.S. and Israeli forces, Tehran remains resilient through increased drone deployment and is preparing for potential ground incursions. These developments carry severe risks for global energy security, with warnings of oil prices reaching $150 per barrel, while simultaneously forcing a recalibration of U.S. domestic security and international diplomatic priorities.

articles.title: Senate Rejects War Powers Measure
articles.summary: The U.S. Senate's rejection of a measure to limit presidential war powers signals a likely escalation of the conflict with Iran, as the administration maintains that military operations are "just getting started." This legislative support for executive action comes amid a broadening battlefield, with rising death tolls in Iran and significant economic disruptions, including spiked shipping insurance costs and threats to global energy and fertilizer supplies. The outcome suggests a period of prolonged regional instability and strained international alliances, as European partners adopt conflicting stances on providing military basing support for U.S. operations.

articles.title: France and UK Send Warships to Mediterranean
articles.summary: The conflict between the U.S.-Israeli coalition and Iran is rapidly escalating and expanding geographically, prompting France and the United Kingdom to deploy warships to the Mediterranean as maritime tensions rise. Key indicators of this expansion include the U.S. destruction of an Iranian vessel, NATO interceptions of Iranian missiles, and a shift in U.S. strategy toward achieving total air superiority over Iran. These developments signal a precarious phase of the conflict that threatens global energy markets and risks widespread regional instability, while highlighting a growing rift between U.S. military objectives and European concerns regarding international law.

articles.title: Trump Says War in Middle East Could Last Weeks
articles.summary: President Trump has signaled that the ongoing conflict with Iran could extend for weeks or longer, marking a significant shift from his previous non-interventionist rhetoric. The administration justifies the military campaign as a preemptive necessity to degrade Iran's ballistic missile and naval capabilities following retaliatory attacks on U.S. embassies and global energy infrastructure. Strategic analysts warn that a protracted engagement could dangerously deplete U.S. munitions stockpiles, potentially creating security vulnerabilities in other regions such as Taiwan while sustaining high volatility in energy markets.

articles.title: War Spreads Across Middle East
articles.summary: The conflict between the United States and Israel against Iran has escalated into a regional war following strikes that reportedly killed Supreme Leader Khamenei and other high-ranking officials. Iran has retaliated by targeting U.S. bases in Kuwait and energy infrastructure in Saudi Arabia and Qatar, causing a significant spike in global oil prices and disrupting maritime traffic in the Strait of Hormuz. While U.S. officials frame the operations as an effort to dismantle Tehran's regional power projection, the instability threatens to draw in neighboring countries and create a volatile power vacuum within the Iranian regime.

Iran has retaliated by targeting U.S. bases in Kuwait and energy infrastructure in Saudi Arabia and Qatar, causing a significant spike in global oil prices and disrupting maritime traffic in the Strait of Hormuz. While U.S. officials frame the operations as an effort to dismantle Tehran's regional power projection, the instability threatens to draw in neighboring countries and create a volatile power vacuum within the Iranian regime.

zh.summary: 美、以與伊朗之間的衝突在據傳導致最高領導人哈米尼及多位高層官員喪生的襲擊後，已升級為區域戰爭。伊朗隨後採取報復行動，針對美國駐科威特基地以及沙烏地阿拉伯與卡達的能源設施發動攻擊，導致全球油價劇烈飆升，並干擾荷姆茲海峽的海上交通。儘管美國官員將此行動定義為瓦解德黑蘭區域武力投射的嘗試，但局勢的不穩定恐將周邊國家捲入其中，並在伊朗政權內部造成動盪的權力真空。

articles.title: Anthropic and Pentagon Clash
articles.summary: Anthropic has rejected a Pentagon ultimatum to authorize its AI technology for unrestricted military use, specifically opposing applications in mass surveillance and fully autonomous weapons. In retaliation, the Defense Department has threatened to terminate a $200 million contract and label the firm a supply chain risk, highlighting the friction between corporate ethics and national security mandates. This standoff reflects a broader global trend where militaries are aggressively adopting AI despite a lack of international consensus on usage guardrails. The incident suggests that the U.S. government may increasingly use tools like the Defense Production Act to compel cooperation from private technology providers.

articles.title: The Shah, the Supreme Leader, the Same Miscalculation
articles.summary: Ray Takeyh argues that both Shah Mohammad Reza Pahlavi and Ayatollah Ali Khamenei failed by assuming they could indefinitely impose their will on the Iranian people while pursuing overextended foreign policies. The Shah's downfall was rooted in forced modernization and excessive military spending, whereas Khamenei’s regime eroded its domestic legitimacy by closing electoral safety valves and exhausting national resources on regional proxies and a failed nuclear program. The eventual destruction of the Islamic Republic’s strategic assets and the death of its leader illustrate that autocratic overreach and the suppression of domestic grievances create inherently unstable systems prone to sudden collapse.

zh.summary: 雷·塔基（Ray Takeyh）指出，穆罕默德·禮薩·巴勒維（Shah Mohammad Reza Pahlavi）與阿里·哈米尼（Ayatollah Ali Khamenei）的共同失敗，在於兩者皆誤以為在追求過度擴張的外交政策時，仍能無限期地將個人意志強加於伊朗人民。巴勒維國王的垮台根植於強制現代化與過度的軍事支出；而哈米尼政權則藉由關閉選舉的安全閥，並將國家資源耗盡於區域代理人與失敗的核計畫，進而侵蝕了其國內合法性。伊斯蘭共和國戰略資產的最終毀滅及其領導人的逝世，說明了專制的過度擴張與對國內民怨的壓制，會造成體制本質上的不穩定，且極易陷入突然的崩潰。

articles.title: The First U.S. Combat Troops Arrive in South Vietnam
articles.summary: This article analyzes the 61st anniversary of the first U.S. combat troop deployment to South Vietnam, highlighting it as the definitive start of the conflict's "Americanization." It provides evidence of how a limited mission for airbase security quickly escalated into a massive military commitment, validating early warnings from officials regarding the irresistible nature of troop demands once combat begins. The analysis serves as a strategic cautionary tale about mission creep, illustrating how initial interventions can fundamentally alter a nation's foreign policy trajectory with long-lasting consequences.

zh.summary: 這篇文章分析了美國向南越派遣首支作戰部隊 61 週年，指出這是該衝突「美國化」的明確開端。文中揭示了最初僅為保護空軍基地的有限任務，如何迅速演變成大規模的軍事介入，證實了早期官員對一旦開戰則增兵需求勢不可擋的預警。這項分析為「任務蔓延」(mission creep) 提供了戰略性的前車之鑑，展現了初步干預如何從根本上扭轉一個國家的外交政策軌跡，並造成深遠影響。

articles.title: How Cross-Border Chinese RMB Flows May Weaken U.S. Sanctions
articles.summary: The article argues that the growth of China’s Cross-Border Interbank Payment System (CIPS) is weakening the effectiveness of U.S. financial sanctions by reducing the visibility of international RMB transactions. While RMB usage on SWIFT appears to be declining, this trend is offset by a 40% increase in direct CIPS participation, which allows banks to bypass SWIFT messaging entirely. This shift undermines the traditional U.S. leverage of threatening to disconnect foreign banks from SWIFT to achieve foreign policy objectives. Consequently, the rising internationalization of the RMB and its independent messaging infrastructure poses a challenge to the dollar's role as a sanctions tool.

articles.title: Morocco’s Free-Trade Zones: A Potential Model for Africa
articles.summary: Morocco is positioning itself as a strategic trade hub through export-oriented free-trade zones and its control of 70% of global phosphate reserves. While these zones drive industrialization and attract significant Western and Chinese investment in sectors like EV batteries and aeronautics, they also serve as a potential conduit for China to circumvent Western tariffs. For U.S. and EU policymakers, Morocco's model highlights the challenge of supporting African infrastructure while mitigating the national security risks associated with Chinese economic expansion.

zh.summary: 摩洛哥正藉由出口導向的自由貿易區以及對全球 70% 磷酸鹽儲量的掌控，將其定位為戰略貿易樞紐。雖然這些貿易區推動了工業化，並吸引西方與中國在電動車電池及航空等領域的大量投資，但它們也成為中國規避西方關稅的潛在管道。對美歐政策制定者而言，摩洛哥模式凸顯了在支持非洲基礎設施建設的同時，如何減輕與中國經濟擴張相關之國家安全風險的挑戰。

articles.title: A “Tear Down the Wall” Moment in Iran Will Damage Both the Islamic Republic—and China
articles.summary: This article advocates for a robust U.S. strategy to support Iranian protesters, arguing that the current unrest presents a unique opportunity to topple the Islamic Republic and strike a blow against Chinese influence. The author contends that the regime's military weakness, exposed by recent U.S. strikes, and its economic failure have emboldened the populace despite Chinese-designed internet suppression tools. To assist the uprising, the piece suggests utilizing kinetic and cyberattacks against Iran's National Information Network to restore protester communications. Successfully weakening Tehran would undermine Beijing’s regional energy access and strategic foothold in the Middle East.

zh.summary: 本文主張美國應採取強勢戰略支持伊朗抗議者，認為當前的動盪是推翻伊斯蘭共和國並打擊中國影響力的獨特契機。作者指出，儘管該政權採用中國設計的網路壓制工具，但近期美國的打擊暴露了其軍事弱點，加上經濟失靈，進而激發了民眾的抗爭勇氣。為協助起義，文中建議針對伊朗的「國家資訊網路」發動動能與網路攻擊，以恢復抗議者的通訊。成功削弱德黑蘭政權將會損害北京在該地區的能源獲取及其在中東的戰略立足點。

articles.title: Go Big, Then Go Smart: Trump, ICE and the Law. How To Skip the Left’s PR Trap
articles.summary: The article contends that the Trump administration must initially assert federal supremacy through the Insurrection Act to dismantle local obstruction of immigration enforcement. It points to escalating violence and non-cooperation from municipal leaders in sanctuary cities as evidence that traditional ICE operations have become high-risk 'PR traps.' To sustain long-term mass deportation goals, the author suggests transitioning to a technology-centric approach that utilizes AI, facial recognition, and inter-agency data sharing to identify targets more subtly and efficiently. This strategy aims to bypass media-driven optics while restoring the normalization of federal law enforcement across the country.

articles.title: The Shrinking Federal Footprint: Education Returns to the States
articles.summary: The report argues that the downsizing and potential closure of the U.S. Department of Education presents an opportunity to return educational authority to states and local communities, thereby reducing federal administrative burdens. Evidence suggests that federal regulations currently drain millions of man-hours into paperwork without demonstrably improving student achievement. To navigate this transition, the authors recommend converting Title I and IDEA funding into flexible state block grants or student-specific micro-savings accounts while empowering states to set their own academic goals. Consequently, state officials must proactively audit federal fund usage and utilize waivers to secure autonomy over curriculum, assessment, and civil rights standards.

articles.title: No Marriage. No Babies. No Future. America’s Going From Birth to Death
articles.summary: The Heritage Foundation argues that the decline of marriage and birthrates represents the most significant existential threat to America’s future, as population growth is projected to reverse by 2030. Citing CBO data and social science, the report asserts that traditional family structures are the primary drivers of national wealth, health, and stability. To counter this demographic collapse, Heritage proposes policy interventions including the elimination of welfare marriage penalties, new tax credits for families, and direct government incentives to prioritize married family formation.

articles.title: Saving America by Saving the Family: A Foundation for the Next 250 Years
articles.summary: This Heritage Foundation report argues that restoring the traditional married family is an existential necessity for American stability and economic growth over the next 250 years. Citing record-low fertility rates and the erosion of marriage due to 1960s-era welfare 'marriage penalties,' the authors present evidence that children in intact, married-parent households achieve significantly better economic and social outcomes. To reverse these trends, the report proposes a 'whole-of-government' strategy featuring new financial incentives, such as the Family and Marriage (FAM) tax credit and Newlywed Early Starters Trust (NEST) accounts, to actively privilege marriage and at-home parenting over alternative arrangements.

articles.title: Tariff Refund Delays Could Cost Taxpayers $700 Million a Month
articles.summary: The Trump administration is attempting to delay the refund of $175 billion in tariffs recently invalidated by the Supreme Court, potentially costing taxpayers $700 million per month in interest. These mandatory interest payments accrue at a rate of approximately $23 million daily, creating a significant fiscal burden while depriving U.S. importers of critical operating capital. Although the Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit recently rejected a government request for a 90-day pause, the ongoing legal maneuvering highlights the high economic cost of administrative resistance to judicial trade rulings. Ultimately, these delays prioritize procedural stalling over fiscal responsibility and the financial health of domestic firms.

articles.title: Clinging to WWII Analogies in Iran War Is Folly
articles.summary: The article argues that the Trump administration's reliance on World War II analogies to frame the conflict with Iran is a strategic error that ignores modern geopolitical realities and specific conflict dynamics. It cites historical failures in WWI and Vietnam to demonstrate how misapplied historical comparisons can blind leaders to actual capabilities and lead to massive, avoidable casualties. The author concludes that pursuing 'unconditional surrender' without clear political objectives or a post-conflict plan risks destroying a government without a viable strategy for what follows.
